facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes

BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies

concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, uniformly positive for CD207/langerin, which is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The patient has a history of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts, which supports this diagnosis.

The patient's bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts, and next-generation sequencing revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes, which is consistent with acute myeloid leukemia.
The patient's skin biopsy showed BRAF-V600E variant status, which is consistent with a BRAF-V600E positive tumor.
The patient's skin biopsy showed a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, which could be consistent with cutaneous lymphoma.

The patient's skin biopsy showed a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, and the patient has a history of myelodysplastic syndrome, which could be consistent with leukemia cutis.

rationales.F05: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F06: The uniform positivity for CD207/langerin is a specific marker for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F08: The presence of the BRAF-V600E variant is a characteristic feature of some cases of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F10: The identification of identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes in both bone marrow and skin biopsy specimens suggests a clonal relationship between the two tissues, supporting a diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis or another myeloid neoplasm.
